title: Our ChatGPT → Tripo → Unreal armour pipeline for MetaHumans works, but fitting is still the bottleneck. How do you handle it?
author: Putrid-Buy-3237
selftext:
Hi all! We're Nordic Wolf Studios, a small studio in Aarhus, Denmark, and we're making Crawling Darkness, a gothic action RPG in Unreal Engine 5.8.3 with MetaHuman heroes. A big part of our gear is made with generative AI, and I wanted to share how we do it and where we're stuck.

Every armour set starts as a concept. We paint the piece onto a mannequin with ChatGPT, getting front, side and back views. Those views go into Tripo, which gives us a 3D mesh. In Unreal we import it, scale and align it automatically, and transfer weights from the MetaHuman body. For simple, rigid pieces like helmets and bracers that already works surprisingly well. The pieces simply follow a bone.

The hard part is anything that has to sit close to the body: chest pieces, shoulders, boots. We use Garment Tool, a plugin from Fab, for skinning, posing and hide masks, and it's good at that. But it doesn't conform the shape to the body. So every set still needs a lot of manual fitting, and it has to be done twice, for the male and the female body. Idle poses look fine, but in attack animations we get gaps and skin poking through at the shoulders, waist and knees.

Two things we learned the hard way:

1. MetaHuman preset outfits delete the body faces under the clothing. So "skin showing through armour" can actually be missing geometry, not a bad fit.

2. Tripo meshes are dense and not built around the MetaHuman topology, so weight transfer is hit and miss until you clean up the mesh first.

So, our question: how do you fit AI-generated or bought clothing onto MetaHumans? Has anyone had luck with proxy cages, a signed-distance "push-out" that conforms a shell to the body before skinning, Mutable or Chaos Outfit, or a Blender shrinkwrap pass? Anything that cuts the per-set manual time would help a lot. We're happy to share our UE Python and Garment Tool scripting in return.

And if you like dark ARPGs: the game is in a free alpha on Windows, with two classes and online co-op for up to four, and we're looking for a few more alpha testers.

If you'd like to talk pipelines, MetaHumans or the game itself, come find us:

\- Website: [https://crawling-darkness.com](https://crawling-darkness.com)

\- Discord: [https://discord.gg/6trrGthM96](https://discord.gg/6trrGthM96)

\- Reddit: [https://www.reddit.com/r/CrawlingDarkness/](https://www.reddit.com/r/CrawlingDarkness/)

Thanks for reading!

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. This is really useful workflow feedback.

The distinction between rigid pieces working well and close-fitting pieces becoming the bottleneck is especially interesting. It sounds like generation itself isn’t really the issue anymore, it’s everything between the generated mesh and something that reliably deforms with the MetaHuman body.

I’d be curious how much of the per-set time is currently going into mesh cleanup versus the actual body fitting/weighting process. That seems like an important distinction if the goal is cutting down the manual work.
